Rashi on Chullin 42a:10:1.hebrew: ובין החיה אשר לא תאכל - אע"פ שחיה, לא תאכל:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:10:1.english: And between the living thing that may not be eaten - Even though it is alive, it may not be eaten.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:10:2.hebrew: שמונה עשרה טרפות - לאו מקרא קמישתמעי, אלא הלכה למשה מסיני הן:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:10:2.english: Eighteen tereifot - They are not learned from a verse, but are a halakha given to Moses at Sinai.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:11:1.english: And there are no more - except eighteen:

Rashi on Chullin 42a:1:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא - כלומר, ואיצטריך רבי אלעזר לאשמועינן דכי יש לו אשה, פסולה, אף על גב דאמרה רבי אלעזר לעיל גבי תמורה:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:1:1.english: Lest you say - That is, Rabbi Elazar needed to teach us that when he has a wife, it is invalid, even though Rabbi Elazar already said it earlier, regarding substitution (temurah).

Rashi on Chullin 42a:1:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא אם איתא דילדה קלא הוה ליה - ומידע ידעי דמשקר:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:1:2.english: Lest you say: If it is so that she gave birth, it would have had publicity - and they would know that he is lying.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:1:4.hebrew: לישנא אחרינא הא דר' אלעזר ור' אבהו לא גרסינן, וה"ג לאתויי עולת יולדת, מהו דתימא אימא ילודי יליד, קמ"ל דאם איתא דאוליד קלא אית לה - ובשיש לו אשה מתוקמא מתניתין, ואיצטריך לתנא למתנייה בזה הכלל, דמהו דתימא ניחוש לה, למאן דחזי סבר בצינעא אוליד, קמ"ל. זה שמעתי, ועיקר הוא. חדא, דהא לא אמרו והאי "מהו דתימא" בכל הנך שמעתתא דאמוראי דלא שאנו דלעיל אמתניתין, דזה הכלל קמא אמרו "מהו דתימא", ואורחא דגמרא למימר "מהו דתימא" אכלל דמתניתין. ועוד, בשאין לו אשה למה ליה למתנייה זה הכלל לאתויי? פשיטא, למאי ניחוש לה:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:1:4.english: Another version: This [statement] of Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Abbahu we do not read; rather, this is the reading: "To include the burnt offering of a woman after childbirth. Lest you say: Say that she gave birth, [but secretly]. It teaches us that if she had given birth, there would be publicity about it" - And the Mishnah is established as [referring to a case] where he has a wife, and the Tanna needed to teach it with this general rule, because [otherwise] you might say: Let us be concerned for her, since whoever sees [that he brings this offering] would think that she gave birth in private. [Therefore] it teaches us [that there is no such concern]. This is what I heard, and it is the main [explanation]. First, because they did not say this "lest you say" in all those statements of the Amoraim, which are not different from those above on the Mishnah; rather, they said "lest you say" on this first general rule, and it is the way of the Gemara to say "lest you say" on a general rule of the Mishnah. And furthermore, if he has no wife, why would [the Tanna] need to teach this general rule to include [this case]? It is obvious — why would we be concerned for her?

Rashi on Chullin 42a:3:1.english: These are tereifot - Any perforation, however small, renders the animal a tereifa.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:3:2.english: Cut - Across its width, [through] the majority of it.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:3:3.hebrew: לבית חללו - ואם לא הגיע לחלל, קתני סיפא דכשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:3:3.english: To its chamber - But if it did not reach the chamber, the latter clause teaches that [the animal] is kosher.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:3:4.hebrew: נשברה השדרה ונפסק החוט - חדא היא, וטרפות דידה משום חוט הוא. ונשברה השדרה דקתני, אורחא דמילתא נקט, דפסיקת החוט ע"י שבירת שדרה היא:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:3:4.english: The spine was broken and the cord was severed - It is one [condition], and its *tereifa* status is on account of the cord. And [the phrase] "the spine was broken" that it teaches, it stated the typical case, for the severing of the cord is through the breaking of the spine.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:1.hebrew: או שחסרה - בגמרא פריך (לקמן חולין דף מז:), היינו נקב:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:1.english: Or that was missing - In the Gemara (below, Chullin 47b) it asks: This is the same as a perforation?

Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:2.hebrew: סמפונות - קנוקנות קטנות המתפשטות בתוך הריאה, שהדם נובע בה כשחותכים אותה:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:2.english: Bronchi - Small tubules that spread out within the lung, from which blood flows when one cuts it.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:3.hebrew: הכרס הפנימית - בגמרא (לקמן חולין נ:) מפרש:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:3.english: The internal rumen - The Gemara explains (below, Chullin 50b):

Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:4.english: That was perforated - With even the slightest [perforation].

Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:5.hebrew: רוב החיצונה - בגמרא (שם דף נ:) מפרש:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:5.english: The majority of the external [rumen] - In the Gemara (there, page 50b) it explains.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:6.hebrew: גדולה וקטנה - לא גסה ודקה קאמר, אלא על [שור] קטן ושור גדול: אם נקרע טפח בשור, אע"ג דלא הוי רובא:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:6.english: Large and small - He does not mean a large animal and a small animal [as in livestock]. Rather, he means a small [ox] and a large ox: if a handbreadth was torn in the ox, even though it is not a majority [of the rumen, it is a tereifa].

Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:8.hebrew: ובית הכוסות - סוף הכרס, שקורין פנצ"א, עשוי ככובע, וקרוי בית הכוסות, והמסס מחובר בו. וסביב סביב לחיבורם, כשאתה מבדילן, יש דופן לזה ודופן לזה, ובאמצע הן שופכין זה לתוך זה. והמאכל נכנס מבית הכוסות להמסס, ומהמסס לקבה, ומהקבה לדקין:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:8.english: And the reticulum - The end of the stomach, which is called pantsa [in Old French], is shaped like a hat and is called the "house of cups" (beit hakosot), and the omasum is attached to it. All around their connection, when you separate them, there is a wall for this one and a wall for that one, and in the middle they empty into one another. The food enters from the reticulum into the omasum, from the omasum into the abomasum, and from the abomasum into the small intestines:

Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:9.hebrew: שניקבו לחוץ - שהנקב נראה מבחוץ, וכגון שניקבו או זה או זה שלא במקום חיבורן. לאפוקי שניקבו במקום חיבורן בשתי דופנותיהן, והנקב הולך מחללו של זה לחללו של זה:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:4:9.english: That were perforated to the outside - That the perforation is visible from the outside, for example where either this one or that one was perforated not at the place of their joining. This excludes where they were perforated at the place of their joining, in both of their walls, and the perforation runs from the cavity of this one to the cavity of that one.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:1.hebrew: נפלה מן הגג - ושחטה מיד, טרפה. אף על פי שאין שבר נראה בה, חוששין שנתרסקו ונתפרקו אבריה, ואין טעם בטרפות, שהלכה למשה מסיני הן. ובגמרא (לקמן חולין דף נא:) אמר שאם שהתה מעת לעת ושחטה, כשרה, ואע"פ שלא עמדה:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:1.english: If it fell from the roof - and it was slaughtered immediately, it is a tereifa. Even though no fracture is visible in it, we are concerned that its limbs were crushed and dislocated. And there is no [rational] reason for the laws of tereifot, for they are a law given to Moses at Sinai. And in the Gemara (below, Chullin 51b) it says that if it remained [alive] for a full day (twenty-four hours) and [then] it was slaughtered, it is kosher, even though it did not stand up.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:10.hebrew: כל שאין כמוה חיה - שלקתה מכה שאין בהמה לקויה דוגמתה ראויה לחיות:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:10.english: Any [animal] that a similar one could not live - That it suffered an injury such that a [similarly] injured animal like it is not able to live.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:2.hebrew: נשתברו רוב צלעותיה - בלא שום נפילה טרפה. ובגמרא (שם דף נב.) מפרש מאי רוב:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:2.english: The majority of its ribs were fractured - Even without any fall, [the animal] is a tereifa. And in the Gemara (there, 52a) it explains what [counts as] a majority.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:3.hebrew: דרוסת הזאב - שהכה בצפרניו ומטיל בה ארס ושורפה. בדקה, אבל בגסה לא אלים זיהריה למיקלייה:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:3.english: Clawed by a wolf - That it struck with its claws and casts venom into it, and burns it. [This applies] to a small [animal]; but in a large [animal], its venom is not strong enough to kill it.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:4.hebrew: ודרוסת ארי בגסה - וכל שכן בדקה. ותנא קמא סבר: אלים זיהריה דזאב, למקלייה נמי לגסה:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:4.english: And one clawed by a lion, in a large [animal] - And all the more so in a small [animal]. And the first Tanna holds: the venom of a wolf is strong enough to kill even a large [animal].

Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:5.english: Hawk - It is espervier (Old French for sparrowhawk).

Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:6.english: In the case of a small bird - [such as] sparrows and doves.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:7.english: And clawed by a large [bird] - ostoir (in Old French).

Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:8.english: In a large bird - Geese and chickens.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:9.hebrew: זה הכלל - בגמרא (לקמן חולין נד.) מפרש לאתויי מאי:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:5:9.english: This is the principle - In the Gemara (below, Chullin 54a) it explains what this comes to include:

Rashi on Chullin 42a:6:1.hebrew: ובשר בשדה טרפה - ואע"ג דילפינן מיניה בעלמא (מכות דף יח.) בשר קדשים שיצא חוץ ממחיצתו, מ"מ טרפה משמע טרפה ממש:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:6:1.english: "And flesh in the field that is torn" - Even though we derive from it elsewhere (Makkot 18a) [the law of] sacrificial flesh that went out beyond its [permitted] boundary, nevertheless "torn" (tereifa) implies an actual tereifa:

Rashi on Chullin 42a:6:2.hebrew: אלא - מנין לטרפה שאין סופה לחיות? לפרושי מתניתין דקתני כל שאין כמוה חיה טרפה, אלמא טרפה אינה חיה:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:6:2.english: Rather - From where [do we derive] that a tereifa will not ultimately live? This is to explain the Mishnah, which teaches, "Any [animal] that one like it cannot live is a tereifa"; evidently, a tereifa cannot live.

Rashi on Chullin 42a:7:1.english: "This is the living thing" - Read it as "this [is a] living thing."

Rashi on Chullin 42a:8:1.hebrew: ולמ"ד טרפה חיה - לקמן בפרקין (חולין דף נז:) אמרו לו, והלא הרבה מתקיימות שתים ושלש שנים:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:8:1.english: And according to the one who says a tereifa can live - Later in this chapter (Chullin 57b) they said to him: But many [animals with a defect] survive two and three years!

Rashi on Chullin 42a:8:2.hebrew: זאת החיה - "זאת" מיעוטא הוא, והכי משמע: זאת, סתם בהמות שהן חיות, אכול:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:8:2.english: “These living things” - “These” is a limiting term, and this is what it means: These — ordinary animals that are alive — you may eat (but not a tereifa).

Rashi on Chullin 42a:8:3.hebrew: חיה אחרת - כגון טרפה, דאע"פ שהיא חיה, לא תאכל:
Rashi on Chullin 42a:8:3.english: Another living thing - For example, a tereifa, which, although it is alive, you may not eat.

Tosafot on Chullin 42a:3:1.hebrew: אלו טרפות - אי גרסינן "אלו", ניחא. ואי גרסינן "ואלו", יש לפרש דקאי אפלוגתא דר' ישבב ור' עקיבא, "והודה לו ר' עקיבא" דנבלה, או קאי אכל הני שחיטתו פסולה דלעיל, דהוה פסול שאירע בשחיטה והוי נבלה, וקאמר הכא: "ואלו הן טרפות":
Tosafot on Chullin 42a:3:1.english: These are tereifot - If we read "These" (eilu), it is fine. But if we read "And these" (ve'eilu), we can explain that it refers either to the dispute between Rabbi Yeshevav and Rabbi Akiva, [where] "Rabbi Akiva agreed with him" that it is a neveilah; or that it refers to all those cases above where the slaughter is invalid, since that is a disqualification that occurred during the slaughter and [the animal] is a neveilah, and [the Mishnah] says here: "And these are tereifot":

Tosafot on Chullin 42a:3:2.hebrew: ניקב הלב לבית חללו - בשאר נקובי לא איצטריך למיתני "לבית חללו", שהן דקין, ופשיטא שאין נקב חשוב בהם כלל אם לא ניקב לבית חללו. אבל לב, שהוא עב, ס"ד שאם ניקב בעומק שהוא חשוב נקב. וניטל הלב והריאה והדקין לא איצטריך למיתני, דבכלל נקובים הוא. דאף על גב דבטחול אמר בגמרא דניטל כשר וניקב טרפה, בכל הני נקובים דתנא פשיטא דכל שכן ניטל. וניקבה המרה נמי נראה דכ"ש ניטל דטריפה. ומ"מ "ניטלה הכבד ולא נשתייר הימנה כלום" איצטריך, דאפשר להיות דניטל כל הכבד ולא המרה, שניטל כל בשר הכבד ונשאר המרה דבוקה בגידי הכבד והסמפונות. והא דתנן (לקמן חולין דף נד.) גבי "ואלו כשרות": "ניקב הלב ולא לבית חללו", צריך לומר דמהכא לא הוה שמעינן, דהוה אמינא ה"ה סמוך לבית חללו דסופו לינקב עד בית החלל. והא דקתני "ניקבה הגרגרת כשרה", היינו משום דבעי למיתני "נסדקה". ו"נשברה השדרה ולא נפסק החוט שלה" איצטריך, דאי מהכא ה"א או הא או הא, אי נמי ה"א דבעיא תרתי, קא משמע לן דבחוט תלי מילתא. ו"ניטל הכבד ולא נשתייר הימנה כזית" פריך בגמרא (לקמן חולין מו.) רישא לסיפא:
Tosafot on Chullin 42a:3:2.english: "The heart was perforated to its chamber" - With the other perforated organs, it was not necessary to teach "to its chamber," for they are thin, and it is obvious that a perforation is not significant in them at all if it did not penetrate to the inner cavity. But the heart, which is thick, I might have thought that if it was perforated in its depth, that counts as a significant perforation. And "the heart was removed," and the lungs, and the intestines, it was not necessary to teach, for it is included in the perforated organs. For although with the spleen the Gemara says that if it was removed it is permitted, but if perforated it is a tereifa, in all these perforated organs that the Tanna taught, it is obvious that all the more so if removed. And if the gallbladder was perforated, it also seems that all the more so if removed, it is a tereifa. In any case, "the liver was removed and nothing remained of it" was necessary [to teach], for it is possible that the entire liver was removed but not the gallbladder, since all the flesh of the liver was removed and the gallbladder remained attached to the veins of the liver and the bronchial tubes. And as for what we learned (below, Chullin 54a) regarding "And these are permitted": "The heart was perforated but not to its chamber," one must say that from here we would not have learned it, for I would have said that the same applies to near its chamber, since it will eventually be perforated through to the cavity. And as for what it teaches, "the windpipe was perforated, it is permitted," that is because it wanted to teach "it was split." And "the spinal column was broken and its cord was not cut" was necessary [to teach], for if [we learned it] from here, I would have said that either this or that [renders it a tereifa], or alternatively I would have said that both are required; it teaches us that the matter depends on the cord. And "the liver was removed and not even an olive's worth of it remained" — the Gemara (below, Chullin 46a) challenges the first clause from the latter clause:

Tosafot on Chullin 42a:4:1.hebrew: או שחסרה - מפרש בגמרא: או שחסרה מבפנים. ולמ"ד חסרון מבפנים לא שמיה חסרון, מפרש: ניקבה לרבנן, או שחסרה לר"ש, דאמר עד שתינקב לבית הסמפונות, ובחסרון כל שהוא מודה:
Tosafot on Chullin 42a:4:1.english: Or that was missing - The Gemara explains: Or that was missing from the inside. And according to the one who says that a deficiency on the inside is not called a deficiency, [the Mishnah] explains: [the phrase] "perforated" is according to the Rabbis, or "missing" is according to Rabbi Shimon, who says [it is not a tereifa] unless it is perforated through to the bronchi, but with regard to a deficiency of any amount he agrees.

Tosafot on Chullin 42a:5:1.hebrew: דרוסת הנץ - גבי טרפות עוף הוא שייך למיתני, אלא משום רבי יהודה תנא ליה הכא:
Tosafot on Chullin 42a:5:1.english: Clawed by a hawk - It belongs to be taught in the context of the *tereifot* of birds; but because of Rabbi Yehuda, [the Tanna] taught it here:

Tosafot on Chullin 42a:5:2.hebrew: דרוסת הנץ - גרסי' בתוספתא [פ"ג] ובערוך [ערך נץ ד'], וכן יסד הפייט בסליחות "תוחלת ישראל": מדרס הגס ונץ, אפרוחים קרוצים. וטעמא לא משום דסופו לינקב, דא"כ בכלל נקובה היא, ומהאי טעמא לא תני במתניתין "דמיא לדיותא" ו"דמיא לבישרא"; אלא טעמא דדרוסה — שהארס שורף וסופה למות:
Tosafot on Chullin 42a:5:2.english: Being clawed by a hawk - This is the reading in the Tosefta [chapter 3] and in the Arukh [entry "nets," 4], and so the liturgical poet composed in the selichah "Tochelet Yisrael": "the trampling of the large one and the hawk, the molded chicks." And the reason is not because it will eventually become perforated, for if so it would already fall under the category of a perforated animal, and for this reason the Mishnah does not teach "it resembles ink" and "it resembles flesh." Rather, the reason for a clawed animal is that the venom burns, and it will ultimately die:

Tosafot on Chullin 42a:9:1.hebrew: זאת החיה מלמד שתפס הקב"ה כל מין ומין והראה למשה - והא דלא חשיב ליה בהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כט.) גבי שלשה דברים שנתקשה משה — מנורה, ראש חדש, ושרצים — ולא חשיב נמי הא דאמר במדרש: כמין מטבע אש הראה הקדוש ברוך הוא למשה, דכתיב "זה יתנו"; שמא לא חשיב אלא מידי דנתקשה. אבל הני, אע"פ שהראהו, לא נתקשה בהן, אלא שתמה על הדבר: מה יוכל אדם ליתן כופר נפשו? הראהו הקב"ה להבחין היטב ולהודיע לישראל. וכן הכא, להראות לישראל איזו היא אסורה ואיזו היא מותרת:
Tosafot on Chullin 42a:9:1.english: "These are the living things" – this teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, seized each and every species and showed it to Moses - And as for the fact that [the Gemara] does not count this in [the chapter] Hakometz Rabbah (Menachot 29a), regarding the three things with which Moses had difficulty — the menorah, the new moon, and the creeping creatures — and it also does not count that which is stated in the Midrash: The Holy One, Blessed be He, showed Moses something like a coin of fire, as it is written, "This they shall give"; perhaps [the Gemara] counts only something with which [Moses] had difficulty. But with these, even though [God] showed him, he did not have difficulty with them; rather, he was astonished at the matter: How can a person give a ransom for his soul? The Holy One, Blessed be He, showed him so that he would discern it well and make it known to Israel. And so too here, [He showed him] in order to show Israel which is forbidden and which is permitted:
